newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai PM sees mild economic recovery in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Thai PM sees mild economic recovery in 1998.

BANGKOK, June 25 (Reuter) - Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said on Wednesday that his government expected a mild economic recovery in 1998 after suffering its worst economic crisis in a decade. Chavalit told a parliamentary debate on the 1997/1998 (October/September) fiscal budget that the Thai gross domestic product would likely expand 5.7 percent in 1998 against revised, expected 5.6 percent growth this year.
The central bank has scaled down its 1997 GDP growth projection several times this year, to 5.9 percent last month from 7.1 percent early this year and against 6.4 percent in 1996.

"The economic slowdown has made it very tough for the government to propose a (balanced, deficit-free) budget...I believe the (1997/1998) austerity budget is appropriate under current economic and bearish financial sector conditions in the country," Chavalit said in his budget statement.

The government proposed to parliament a trimmed 982 billion baht ($39.3 billion) budget next year, a small four percent rise from this year. The planned expenditure is 26.59 billion baht lower than what it hoped to spend earier. Thailand is facing its first budget deficit in a decade due to a sharp reduction in tax revenue caused by the economic slowdown.
